basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: How an order or obligation is fulfilled, not the order itself.
Covers goods, services, digital content and access.
Differs from a shipment, which is a transport movement.
Keeps dispatch, handover, receipt, inspection and acceptance separate.

may: Plan and track fulfilment units and stages.
Record dispatch and handover events from sources.
Reconcile fulfilment with orders and invoices.
mustNot: Accept obligations or allocate inventory without delegation.

considerations: Failed delivery of essential goods or services harms people who depend on them.
Delivery addresses and recipient data are personal.
Courier and warehouse workers face time pressure from tracking metrics.

items: A fulfilment names an order or obligation, items, quantities, a recipient and stage events.
Often confused with a shipment, an order, an invoice or a delivery note.
